title: "Sequence Sensitivity Explorer"
subtitle: "Same frames, different order — see how the score changes"
format:

    page-layout: full
---

Build a 9-frame sequence by clicking the buttons below. Frame 10 is fixed as an open frame (5, 4) to isolate the effect of frame ordering. Both scores update live.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false

// ── Scoring functions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function scoreTraditional(balls) {
  let score = 0;
  let i = 0;
  for (let frame = 0; frame < 10; frame++) {
    if (i >= balls.length) return null;
    if (frame < 9) {
      if (balls[i] === 10) {
        if (i + 2 >= balls.length) return null;
        score += 10 + balls[i+1] + balls[i+2];
        i += 1;
      } else {
        if (i + 1 >= balls.length) return null;
        score += balls[i] + balls[i+1];
        if (balls[i] + balls[i+1] === 10) {
          if (i + 2 >= balls.length) return null;
          score += balls[i+2];
        }
        i += 2;
      }
    } else {
      if (balls[i] === 10) {
        if (i + 2 >= balls.length) return null;
        score += 10 + balls[i+1] + balls[i+2];
      } else {
        if (i + 1 >= balls.length) return null;
        if (balls[i] + balls[i+1] === 10) {
          if (i + 2 >= balls.length) return null;
          score += 10 + balls[i+2];
        } else {
          score += balls[i] + balls[i+1];
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return score;
}

function scoreWorld(balls) {
  let score = 0;
  let i = 0;
  for (let frame = 0; frame < 10; frame++) {
    if (i >= balls.length) return null;
    if (balls[i] === 10) {
      score += 30;
      i += 1;
    } else {
      if (i + 1 >= balls.length) return null;
      if (balls[i] + balls[i+1] === 10) {
        score += 10 + balls[i];
      } else {
        score += balls[i] + balls[i+1];
      }
      i += 2;
    }
  }
  return score;
}

// ── State ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

viewof frames = {
  const container = html`<div style="margin-bottom: 20px;">
    <h3>Your 9-frame sequence:</h3>
    <div id="frame-display" style="display: flex; gap: 8px; flex-wrap: wrap; margin-bottom: 15px; min-height: 50px;"></div>
    <div style="margin-bottom: 10px;">
      <strong>Add a frame:</strong>
    </div>
    <div>
      <button class="frame-btn strike" onclick="addFrame('strike')">Strike (X)</button>
      <button class="frame-btn spare" onclick="addFrame('spare55')">Spare (5,5)</button>
      <button class="frame-btn spare" onclick="addFrame('spare73')">Spare (7,3)</button>
      <button class="frame-btn spare" onclick="addFrame('spare91')">Spare (9,1)</button>
      <button class="frame-btn open" onclick="addFrame('open54')">Open (5,4)</button>
      <button class="frame-btn open" onclick="addFrame('open81')">Open (8,1)</button>
      <button class="frame-btn open" onclick="addFrame('open32')">Open (3,2)</button>
    </div>
    <div style="margin-top: 10px;">
      <button onclick="undoFrame()" style="padding: 6px 16px; margin-right: 8px;">Undo</button>
      <button onclick="clearFrames()" style="padding: 6px 16px;">Clear All</button>
    </div>
  </div>`;

  let currentFrames = [];

  const frameLabels = {
    'strike': 'X',
    'spare55': '5/',
    'spare73': '7/',
    'spare91': '9/',
    'open54': '5,4',
    'open81': '8,1',
    'open32': '3,2'
  };

  const frameBalls = {
    'strike': [10],
    'spare55': [5, 5],
    'spare73': [7, 3],
    'spare91': [9, 1],
    'open54': [5, 4],
    'open81': [8, 1],
    'open32': [3, 2]
  };

  function frameColor(type) {
    if (type === 'strike') return '#1a1a1a';
    if (type.startsWith('spare')) return '#888888';
    return '#cccccc';
  }

  function render() {
    const display = container.querySelector('#frame-display');
    display.innerHTML = '';
    currentFrames.forEach((f, i) => {
      const el = html`<div style="
        padding: 10px 16px;
        border-radius: 6px;
        background: ${frameColor(f)};
        color: ${f.startsWith('open') ? 'black' : 'white'};
        font-weight: bold;
        font-size: 1.1em;
        text-align: center;
        min-width: 40px;
      ">F${i+1}<br>${frameLabels[f]}</div>`;
      display.appendChild(el);
    });
    if (currentFrames.length < 9) {
      const remaining = html`<div style="
        padding: 10px 16px; border: 2px dashed #ccc; border-radius: 6px;
        color: #999; text-align: center; min-width: 40px;
      ">F${currentFrames.length + 1}<br>?</div>`;
      display.appendChild(remaining);
    }
    // Always show frame 10
    const f10 = html`<div style="
      padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 6px;
      background: #f0f0f0; border: 1px solid #ccc;
      color: #666; text-align: center; min-width: 40px;
    ">F10<br>5,4</div>`;
    display.appendChild(f10);

    container.value = [...currentFrames];
    container.dispatchEvent(new Event("input"));
  }

  window.addFrame = function(type) {
    if (currentFrames.length < 9) {
      currentFrames.push(type);
      render();
    }
  };

  window.undoFrame = function() {
    currentFrames.pop();
    render();
  };

  window.clearFrames = function() {
    currentFrames = [];
    render();
  };

  render();
  return container;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false

frameBallsMap = ({
  'strike': [10],
  'spare55': [5, 5],
  'spare73': [7, 3],
  'spare91': [9, 1],
  'open54': [5, 4],
  'open81': [8, 1],
  'open32': [3, 2]
})

balls = {
  if (frames.length < 9) return null;
  let b = [];
  for (let f of frames) {
    b = b.concat(frameBallsMap[f]);
  }
  b = b.concat([5, 4]); // frame 10
  return b;
}

tradScore = balls ? scoreTraditional(balls) : null
worldScore = balls ? scoreWorld(balls) : null
```

## How to use

1. Click frame buttons to build a 9-frame sequence
2. Watch both scores update as you reach 9 frames
3. Try reordering the same frames — click **Clear All** and enter them in a different order
4. Notice: World Bowling always gives the same score for the same frame composition, regardless of order. Traditional scoring changes.

## Try these experiments

**Experiment 1: Strike placement matters**

- Enter: X, X, X, X, X, 5/, 5/, 5/, 5/ — note both scores
- Clear and enter: 5/, 5/, 5/, 5/, X, X, X, X, X — note the traditional score changes, World Bowling stays the same

**Experiment 2: Consecutive vs scattered strikes**

- Enter: X, X, X, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4
- Clear and enter: X, 5,4, X, 5,4, X, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4
- Same three strikes, but consecutive strikes score higher under traditional scoring

**Experiment 3: The commutativity proof in action**

- Enter any 9 frames you like and note the World Bowling score
- Rearrange them in any order — the World Bowling score is always the same
- This is Proposition 1 from the paper: World Bowling is commutative
